prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of optical lattice clocks, in which neutral atoms trapped at a magic wavelength reach accuracy and stability near 1e-18

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: optical lattice clocks for Katori and Ye. The criterion I apply is the one I stated publicly, a discovery or invention with an identifiable origin and identifiable people. Katori's magic-wavelength proposal removed the trap-induced shift that blocked neutral-atom optical clocks, and Ye's group took the scheme to roughly 1e-18, beyond the caesium definition of the second. Several independent laboratories with strontium, ytterbium and other species have reproduced it, and it already yields relativistic-redshift measurements and limits on varying constants. The round-1 exchange sharpened my view that this is the only leading candidate where scientific maturity and a defensible two-name credit coincide. The citation should name the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and not optical clocks in general, which answers the chair's first question and separates it from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize. I would not lean on the pending redefinition of the second in the wording. Weighing measurement capability against conceptual novelty, I do not think either should decide the matter alone, so I rest on the combination of a distinct invention, independent confirmation and a clean credit boundary.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is still the overlap with 2005 and 2012, and it is a judgement and not a settled fact: a reader who sees the lattice clock as a continuation of precision spectroscopy would regard the area as already honoured. Other lattice-clock contributors (Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Derevianko) and the ion-clock groups fall outside two names, and the relative weight of Katori's proposal against Ye's accuracy programme remains unresolved. I also recognise that a prize for a measurement instrument may be weighed below a new classification of matter, which is the core of the B047 case, and that the redefinition of the second has not yet happened. I rely on recollection of the priority history of the magic-wavelength proposal and have not verified it from documents.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B047 for Kane, Mele and Molenkamp: a stable Z2 interpretation confirmed over fifteen to twenty years, with a theory-plus-experiment trio, while accepting that the 2016 overlap and the omission of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Hasan are real.
responses.response: I agree the Z2 classification is a clean and original step and that the interpretation is mature. My reservation is the one he lists himself: after reading the chair's summary, Mele versus Hasan, the missing Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the 2016 topological-phases prize are three open questions at once, and I have not seen an argument that closes the 2016 overlap other than careful citation wording. I do not hold that against the science. It is why I keep B047 as my first alternative and not my lead, and I would not oppose it if the allocation can be settled without a name I cannot defend.

responses.point: Mehlig treats B047 as a conceptual change, a topological invariant replacing broken symmetry, and raises a two-part configuration pairing it with a precision or quantum-technology achievement, without endorsing a split.
responses.response: I take the conceptual weight seriously, but I do not think B047 should be paired with B010 as a two-part prize merely to avoid choosing. A two-part configuration would still need each part to be settled on its own, and B047's credit is not settled. It would also divide a prize between a conceptual classification and a measurement invention without a shared scientific theme, which I find hard to justify. If the committee settles B047's names, I would rather it be decided on its own merits against B010 than as a compromise.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B051, a prediction in 2011 followed by experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in 2018, concedes that the pairing mechanism is unsettled and Cao is outside the names, and lists B047 and B010 as the safer options.
responses.response: I accept that a prize can honour a phenomenon before its mechanism is understood, and his prediction-then-confirmation argument is the right test. But the same test also asks who exactly did the original work, and the first author of the 2018 experiments is outside the trio while other groups made independent contributions. A citation that honours the states without asserting a mechanism helps on interpretation but not on credit. I would keep B051 as an alternative and revisit it in a few years, and I note that he himself calls B010 and B047 the more mature choices.

responses.point: Kroll supports B010 and discloses a doctoral-period stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, asking the committee whether this requires recusal on B010.
responses.response: I think the disclosure is properly made, and the connection is to the 2005 comb work, adjacent to but not part of the lattice-clock credit, so I would not by itself treat it as disqualifying. The committee should note it and let the chair decide. It does matter for how we count: his support does not change my own reasoning, which rests on the magic-wavelength scheme and independent reproduction, but it means B010 should not be presented as having four unconditional supporters if he withholds.

responses.point: Lindroth would not lean on the pending redefinition of the second in the citation and, with Kroll, says the committee need not rank Katori's proposal against Ye's accuracy programme.
responses.response: I now agree more firmly and have changed the citation accordingly: it names the lattice scheme and the 1e-18 performance but no longer mentions the redefinition of the second. I also agree that the committee need not rank proposal over accuracy; both are needed for the invention to be a working instrument, and no member has shown that a different pair would be better.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the lattice clock as distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize; this rests on citation wording.
How to treat other lattice-clock pioneers and ion-clock groups outside the two-name credit; I rely on recollection of the priority history, not verified documentation.
Whether B047's allocation (Mele versus Hasan, and the absent Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal) can be settled, since that would make it a stronger competitor than I currently judge.
Whether the final count should be read with Kroll's disclosure in mind.
statement.conflict_note: I disclosed in round 1 a professional proximity to transmission electron microscopy (B039) and would recuse from any decision on it; I have not led with it and it is not in my configuration or alternatives. Göran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, relevant to a conflict check on B041, which I do not support. I have no connection to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer apparent from my profile. No new disclosure arises from round 1.
